title: Apollo 11 Moon Landing
text: The Apollo 11 mission landed the first humans on the Moon on July 20 1969. Commander Neil Armstrong and lunar module pilot Buzz Aldrin formed the American crew that landed the Apollo Lunar Module Eagle.

title: Eiffel Tower Construction
text: The Eiffel Tower is a wrought-iron lattice tower on the Champ de Mars in Paris France. Constructed from 1887 to 1889 as the entrance arch to the 1889 World's Fair it was designed by engineer Gustave Eiffel.

title: Plant Photosynthesis
text: Photosynthesis is a biological process used by plants and other organisms to convert light energy into chemical energy. In green plants photosynthesis takes place inside chloroplasts containing chlorophyll pigments.

title: Python Programming Language
text: Python is a high-level general-purpose programming language created by Guido van Rossum and first released in 1991. Its design philosophy emphasizes code readability with the use of significant indentation.

title: Theory of General Relativity
text: Albert Einstein published the theory of general relativity in 1915. It describes gravity not as a conventional force but as the curvature of spacetime caused by the uneven distribution of mass and energy.

title: Great Wall of China
text: The Great Wall of China is a series of fortifications built across the historical northern borders of ancient Chinese states and Imperial China as protection against nomadic groups. Construction began during the Qin dynasty.

title: Discovery of DNA Structure
text: The double helix molecular structure of DNA was discovered in 1953 by James Watson and Francis Crick utilizing critical X-ray diffraction data produced by Rosalind Franklin and Maurice Wilkins.

title: Turing Machine Model
text: A Turing machine is a mathematical model of computation describing an abstract machine that manipulates symbols on a strip of tape according to a table of rules. It was invented in 1936 by Alan Turing.

title: Mount Everest Geography
text: Mount Everest is Earth's highest mountain above sea level located in the Mahalangur Himal sub-range of the Himalayas. The China-Nepal border runs across its summit point at an elevation of 8848.86 meters.

title: Discovery of Penicillin
text: Penicillin was discovered in 1928 by Scottish physician and microbiologist Alexander Fleming after he noticed that a green mold Penicillium notatum had contaminated a Petri dish and lysed surrounding bacteria.

title: Transformer Architecture
text: The Transformer neural network architecture was introduced in 2017 in the research paper Attention Is All You Need by Vaswani et al. It relies entirely on self-attention mechanisms without recurrence or convolutions.

title: Speed of Light
text: The speed of light in vacuum commonly denoted c is a universal physical constant exactly equal to 299792458 meters per second approximately 300000 kilometers per second.

title: Human Heart Anatomy
text: The human heart is a muscular organ with four chambers: two upper atria and two lower ventricles. Deoxygenated blood enters the right atrium while oxygenated blood from the lungs enters the left atrium.

title: World Wide Web Invention
text: The World Wide Web was invented by British computer scientist Tim Berners-Lee in 1989 while working at CERN. The first web browser and web server were released outside CERN in 1991.

title: Hubble Space Telescope
text: The Hubble Space Telescope was launched into low Earth orbit in 1990 aboard the Space Shuttle Discovery. It was built by NASA with contributions from the European Space Agency ESA.

title: Plate Tectonics Theory
text: Plate tectonics is the scientific theory explaining the large-scale motion of seven large plates and the movements of a larger number of smaller plates of Earth's lithosphere over the asthenosphere.

title: Deep Blue vs Kasparov
text: In May 1997 IBM's Deep Blue supercomputer defeated World Chess Champion Garry Kasparov in a six-game match under standard tournament time controls marking a milestone in artificial intelligence.

title: CRISPR-Cas9 Genome Editing
text: CRISPR-Cas9 is a genome editing technology adapted from a naturally occurring bacterial defense mechanism against bacteriophages pioneered by Jennifer Doudna and Emmanuelle Charpentier.

title: Saturn's Ring System
text: Saturn has an extensive planetary ring system consisting of nine continuous main rings and three discontinuous arcs composed mostly of water ice with a trace component of rocky debris.

title: Transistor Invention
text: The point-contact transistor was invented in December 1947 by John Bardeen Walter Brattain and William Shockley at Bell Telephone Laboratories ushering in modern solid-state electronics.
